answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The tundra multiplier is published, charged in ripple, and lotus lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4690 identities would post 1451 proofs and burn roughly 20 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
